placements.title: A deployment gate moves from incident-driven concern to a ratified, scoped, owned operational requirement
placements.frame: Is this expressing a deployment control that is already in force — declared, scoped, and owned — and what past failure is cited as the reason it now exists?
placements.why: src-1, src-3, src-4, and src-5 together perform one enactment — a signed-release-manifest gate stated as already required, then respecified in structured Gate/Scope/Owner form, spanning staging and production and assigned to Quinton Fairweather as owner. src-2 is the fact-grade incident (two unsigned artifacts reaching staging) that motivates the gate; per the narrative-grain rule it is evidence for this theme rather than its own leaf, since the future-facing subject future envelopes will keep feeding is the gate-as-control theme, not the one-time incident. No existing leaf in the supplied graph (Diagnostic First Methodology, Knowledge Gap Mapping) touches deployment governance, so this names a genuinely new subject.
